questions.e: The levonorgestrel intrauterine system is the first-line treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding without structural pathology and also gives contraception. Tranexamic acid reduces bleeding but is not contraceptive, and ablation requires that the woman has completed her family.

questions.s: A couple attends a clinic in Lahore with concern about fertility. How is infertility usually defined?
o: Failure to conceive after 3 months of regular intercourse
Failure to conceive after 6 months of contraception use
Failure to carry a pregnancy beyond 12 weeks
Failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse
questions.e: Infertility is failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; earlier evaluation is reasonable in women over 35 or with known risk factors. Failure to carry a pregnancy is recurrent pregnancy loss rather than infertility.

questions.s: A 28-year-old woman with a regular 28-day cycle is being investigated for infertility. Which test best confirms that she ovulates?
questions.e: A mid-luteal serum progesterone, on day 21 of a 28-day cycle, confirms ovulation when it is raised. FSH and AMH assess ovarian reserve rather than ovulation, and temperature charts are unreliable.

questions.s: The husband of a woman being investigated for infertility is tall with small firm testes and gynaecomastia. Semen analysis shows azoospermia. FSH and LH are raised and testosterone is low. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Azoospermia with small testes, high gonadotropins and low testosterone indicates primary testicular failure, classically 47,XXY Klinefelter syndrome. Kallmann syndrome causes low gonadotropins, and obstruction gives normal-sized testes and normal hormones.

questions.s: A 30-year-old woman with infertility had pelvic inflammatory disease treated 4 years ago and has occasional pelvic pain. Her ovulation and her husband's semen analysis are normal. What is the most appropriate test of tubal patency?
questions.e: Women with a history suggesting pelvic pathology, such as PID or endometriosis, should have laparoscopy and dye so that tubal and peritoneal disease can be assessed and treated together. Hysterosalpingography is used for women without known comorbidities.

questions.s: Six days after hCG trigger in an IVF cycle, a 27-year-old with PCOS develops abdominal distension, nausea and breathlessness. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries and ascites. Haematocrit is 48 %. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Adnexal torsion of the left ovary
questions.e: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome follows hCG exposure in stimulated cycles, with enlarged ovaries, fluid shift into the third space causing ascites and haemoconcentration; women with PCOS are at higher risk. Torsion causes sudden severe unilateral pain rather than ascites and haemoconcentration.

questions.s: Rubina, 30, from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, has 5 years of primary infertility and scanty periods. Hysterosalpingography shows beaded tubes with rigid, pipe-stem appearance and a distorted cavity. Endometrial biopsy shows caseating granulomas. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Genital tuberculosis is an important cause of infertility in Pakistan; it usually spreads to the tubes from a distant focus, giving beaded, rigid tubes, and endometrial involvement causes oligomenorrhoea. Caseating granulomas confirm the diagnosis, and anti-tuberculous therapy is required.

questions.s: A 24-year-old woman on a 21-day combined oral contraceptive pill forgot to take one pill in the middle of the second week of her packet. She remembered 30 hours later. What is the most appropriate advice?
o: Take the missed pill now and continue as usual
Stop the pack and start a new one after 7 days
Use emergency contraception and condoms for 7 days
Discard the pack and switch to the progestogen-only pill
questions.e: Missing one combined pill (less than 48 hours since it was due) does not reduce protection; she should take it as soon as remembered and continue normally. Extra precautions and possible emergency contraception are needed when two or more pills are missed.

questions.s: A 26-year-old woman had unprotected intercourse 4 days ago. She is mid-cycle and wants the most effective emergency contraception. She has no contraindications. What is the most appropriate option?
o: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken twice
questions.e: The copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraceptive and can be inserted up to 5 days after unprotected intercourse; it then provides ongoing contraception. Levonorgestrel is less effective and licensed for 72 hours.

questions.s: A 28-year-old woman requests the combined oral contraceptive pill. Which feature in her history is an absolute contraindication?
questions.e: Migraine with aura raises the risk of ischaemic stroke with combined oestrogen-containing contraception, so it is an absolute contraindication (UKMEC 4). Previous ectopic and anaemia are not contraindications; the combined pill reduces menstrual blood loss.

questions.s: Samina, 25, has just started a rifampicin-containing regimen for pulmonary tuberculosis. She wants reliable contraception for the next 6 months. What is the most appropriate method?
questions.e: Rifampicin is a strong liver enzyme inducer that reduces the efficacy of oral hormonal methods and the implant. The copper IUD is unaffected; DMPA injection or the LNG-IUS are also acceptable.

questions.s: A woman plans to conceive in about a year and asks about contraception until then. Which method is associated with the longest delay in return of fertility after stopping?
questions.e: After stopping the DMPA injection, return of fertility can be delayed by up to a year. Fertility returns quickly after removal of an IUD or stopping the combined pill.

questions.s: A 33-year-old woman had a copper IUD inserted 2 years ago. At review the threads cannot be seen in the cervical os. Pregnancy test is negative. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Reassure and review in a year
Remove the device by hysteroscopy immediately
Abdominal X-ray as the first test
Pelvic ultrasound to locate the device
questions.e: With missing threads, pregnancy should be excluded and alternative contraception advised until a pelvic ultrasound locates the device. An X-ray is used only if ultrasound does not show the device in the uterus, to look for perforation.

questions.s: What is the principal mode of contraceptive action of the traditional levonorgestrel progestogen-only pill?
o: Inhibition of fertilisation by spermicidal action
questions.e: Traditional progestogen-only pills act mainly by thickening cervical mucus, which blocks sperm penetration; ovulation is inhibited in only some cycles. Desogestrel pills, in contrast, inhibit ovulation in most cycles.

questions.s: Ayesha, 22, has periods every 2 to 3 months, acne and excess facial hair. BMI is 29. Testosterone is mildly raised, prolactin and TSH are normal and the 17-hydroxyprogesterone is normal. Ultrasound shows enlarged ovaries with multiple peripheral follicles. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Oligomenorrhoea, clinical and biochemical hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovarian morphology meet the Rotterdam criteria for PCOS once other causes are excluded. A normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone makes non-classic CAH unlikely, and mild testosterone elevation argues against a tumour.

questions.s: A 34-year-old woman with long-standing PCOS has only 2 to 3 periods a year and is not on any treatment. Which long-term risk is directly related to her infrequent periods?
o: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix
questions.e: Chronic anovulation exposes the endometrium to unopposed oestrogen, increasing the risk of hyperplasia and endometrial carcinoma; a withdrawal bleed at least every 3 to 4 months or the LNG-IUS protects the endometrium. Women with PCOS are not oestrogen-deficient, so osteoporosis is not a particular risk.

questions.s: A 26-year-old woman has developed rapidly progressive hirsutism, deepening of the voice and clitoromegaly over 4 months. Serum testosterone is more than three times the upper limit of normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Rapid onset of virilisation with very high testosterone suggests an androgen-secreting ovarian or adrenal tumour and requires imaging. PCOS causes gradual hirsutism with only mildly raised testosterone and no virilisation.

questions.s: A 28-year-old woman with PCOS and a BMI of 33 wants to become pregnant. She has irregular periods. What is the most appropriate first-line advice?
o: Weight loss through diet and exercise
Bilateral wedge resection of the ovaries
questions.e: In overweight women with PCOS, a weight loss of 5 to 10 % can restore ovulation and improves pregnancy outcomes, so lifestyle change is the first step before ovulation induction. Surgical options and IVF are second- or third-line.

questions.s: A 20-year-old unmarried student with PCOS is troubled by irregular periods and facial hair. She does not want pregnancy now. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
questions.e: The combined pill regulates cycles, protects the endometrium and reduces ovarian androgen production and free testosterone, improving hirsutism and acne. Clomifene induces ovulation and is for women trying to conceive; spironolactone must be used with reliable contraception because it is teratogenic.

questions.s: A 30-year-old woman with PCOS has a BMI of 31 and a family history of type 2 diabetes. Her fasting glucose is 98 mg/dL. Which additional test best assesses her glucose tolerance?
questions.e: Women with PCOS, particularly with obesity or a family history, have high rates of impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes; an OGTT detects impaired tolerance missed by fasting glucose. Serum insulin levels are not used diagnostically.

questions.s: Kausar, 38, has heavy prolonged periods for 2 years. Abdominal examination finds a firm, irregular, non-tender mass arising from the pelvis, equivalent to a 16-week pregnancy. Pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Fibroids (leiomyomas) cause an irregularly enlarged, firm, non-tender uterus with heavy menstrual bleeding. Adenomyosis gives a symmetrically enlarged, often tender uterus with painful periods.

questions.s: A 27-year-old woman at 20 weeks of gestation, known to have a 6 cm intramural fibroid, develops acute localised abdominal pain over the fibroid with a temperature of 37.9 °C and mild leucocytosis. There is no bleeding and the fetus is well. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Red (carneous) degeneration is haemorrhagic infarction of a fibroid, most common in the second trimester, presenting with localised pain, tenderness and low-grade fever; it is managed with rest and analgesia. Torsion only occurs with pedunculated fibroids.

questions.s: A 36-year-old woman with a 12 cm fibroid and Hb 8.9 g/dL is scheduled for abdominal myomectomy in 3 months. She is given a GnRH agonist before surgery. What is the main aim of this treatment?
o: To prevent recurrence of fibroids after surgery
To convert the fibroid into a pedunculated form
To shrink the fibroid and allow Hb to recover
questions.e: Preoperative GnRH agonists induce amenorrhoea, allowing Hb to rise, and shrink fibroids, which can reduce blood loss and allow a smaller incision. Fibroids regrow after the treatment stops, so it does not prevent recurrence.

questions.s: A 32-year-old woman with 2 years of infertility and heavy periods has a 2.5 cm submucous fibroid distorting the uterine cavity on ultrasound. Other infertility tests are normal. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: Submucous fibroids distorting the cavity reduce fertility and cause heavy bleeding, and hysteroscopic resection improves both while preserving the uterus. Embolisation is not recommended for women wishing to conceive, and GnRH agonists prevent pregnancy while used.

questions.s: A 61-year-old woman, postmenopausal for 10 years and not on hormone therapy, has a known uterine fibroid that has grown rapidly over 6 months, with new pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding. What is the most concerning diagnosis?
questions.e: Fibroids normally shrink after menopause, so rapid growth in a postmenopausal woman suggests leiomyosarcoma, which needs urgent assessment. Hyaline degeneration and calcification are benign changes, and red degeneration occurs mainly in pregnancy.

questions.s: Which type of uterine fibroid is most likely to cause heavy menstrual bleeding even when it is small?
questions.e: Submucous fibroids project into the cavity, increase the endometrial surface area and interfere with haemostasis, so even small ones cause heavy bleeding. Subserous fibroids grow outward and mainly cause pressure symptoms.

questions.s: Bibi, 62, para 7, complains of a dragging sensation and a mass at the vaginal opening that is worse on straining and at the end of the day. Examination shows descent of the cervix to the introitus. What is the most important risk factor for her condition?
questions.e: Vaginal childbirth, especially multiple, prolonged or instrumental deliveries, damages pelvic floor muscles, ligaments and nerves and is the main risk factor for uterovaginal prolapse; menopause, obesity and chronic cough contribute. Caesarean birth is protective compared with vaginal birth.

questions.s: An 82-year-old woman with severe heart failure has a symptomatic second-degree uterine prolapse. She is not fit for surgery. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: A vaginal pessary is an effective non-surgical option for women unfit for or declining surgery, and is checked and changed regularly. All the other options are operations.

questions.s: Which structures provide the main level I support of the uterus and upper vagina, preventing uterine prolapse?
questions.e: The cardinal (transverse cervical) and uterosacral ligaments suspend the cervix and upper vagina and provide level I support; their weakening leads to uterine descent. The round ligaments mainly maintain anteversion and give little support against prolapse.

questions.s: A 45-year-old para 4 leaks small amounts of urine when she coughs, sneezes or lifts. She has no urgency or frequency. Urine dipstick is normal. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
o: Supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least 3 months
questions.e: Stress urinary incontinence is treated first with supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least 3 months; surgery is considered if this fails. Antimuscarinics such as oxybutynin treat urge incontinence from an overactive bladder.

questions.s: Ten days after a home delivery following 2 days of obstructed labour in rural Balochistan, a 19-year-old woman reports constant leakage of urine from the vagina day and night. She does not void normally. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Prolonged obstructed labour causes pressure necrosis of the bladder base against the pubis, leading to a vesicovaginal fistula with continuous urinary leakage about 1 to 2 weeks later. Stress incontinence is intermittent and provoked by raised abdominal pressure.

questions.s: Which infection is the main cause of cervical cancer?
questions.e: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus, mainly types 16 and 18, causes most cervical cancers, which is the basis for HPV vaccination and HPV-based screening. HSV-2 was once suspected but is not a cause.

questions.s: Shamim, 45, has had post-coital bleeding for 3 months. Speculum examination shows a friable, irregular growth on the cervix that bleeds on touch. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.e: A visible suspicious cervical lesion needs a biopsy for histological diagnosis; cytology is a screening test for asymptomatic women and may be falsely negative with an obvious tumour. Treating as infection delays the diagnosis.

questions.s: A 50-year-old woman has squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix extending to the pelvic side wall, with hydronephrosis on CT. What is the standard primary treatment?
questions.e: Locally advanced cervical cancer (stage IIB and beyond, including side wall involvement or hydronephrosis) is treated with external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy with concurrent cisplatin. Radical hysterectomy is for early-stage disease confined to the cervix.

questions.s: A 52-year-old woman taking tamoxifen for breast cancer asks about side effects. Which gynaecological condition does tamoxifen most increase the risk of?
questions.e: Tamoxifen acts as an oestrogen agonist on the endometrium in postmenopausal women and increases the risk of endometrial hyperplasia, polyps and carcinoma, so any abnormal bleeding needs investigation. It is not associated with cervical or ovarian cancer.

questions.s: A 35-year-old woman's mother and sister both had ovarian cancer in their forties. Which inherited condition most likely explains this family history?
questions.e: BRCA1 mutations carry the highest lifetime risk of epithelial ovarian cancer, often at younger ages, along with breast cancer. Lynch syndrome also increases ovarian risk but is mainly associated with colorectal and endometrial cancers.

questions.s: A 19-year-old woman has a 10 cm solid ovarian mass on ultrasound. Serum LDH is markedly raised, while AFP and beta-hCG are normal. What is the most likely tumour?
questions.e: Dysgerminoma is the commonest malignant germ cell tumour in young women and typically raises LDH. Yolk sac tumours secrete AFP and choriocarcinoma secretes hCG, while mature cystic teratomas are usually cystic with fat and calcification.

questions.s: A 74-year-old woman with long-standing vulval itching and white, thin, crinkled vulval skin now has a painless ulcerated lump on the right labium majus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva
questions.e: Lichen sclerosus (white, thin, itchy skin) is a precursor of vulval squamous cell carcinoma in older women, which presents as a lump or ulcer and needs biopsy. A Bartholin abscess is painful and in the posterior labium in younger women.

questions.s: A 28-year-old woman has a thin, grey, homogeneous vaginal discharge with a fishy odour, without itching. Vaginal pH is 5.0 and microscopy shows clue cells. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: Thin grey fishy discharge, pH above 4.5 and clue cells meet the criteria for bacterial vaginosis, treated with metronidazole. Fluconazole treats candidiasis, which causes itchy white curd-like discharge with normal pH.

questions.s: A 25-year-old at 24 weeks of gestation has vulval itching and a thick white curd-like discharge. Microscopy shows pseudohyphae. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: Vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy is treated with a topical imidazole such as clotrimazole, often for a longer course; oral azoles are avoided in pregnancy. Metronidazole treats bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis.

questions.s: A 30-year-old woman has a profuse, frothy, yellow-green offensive vaginal discharge with vulval soreness. Speculum examination shows punctate haemorrhages on the cervix. Wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms. Apart from treating her, what is most important?
questions.e: Trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection, treated with metronidazole for the woman and her partner to prevent reinfection. The strawberry cervix is due to infection and does not need colposcopy.

questions.s: A 23-year-old woman has lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia and fever of 38 °C. Examination shows cervical motion tenderness and bilateral adnexal tenderness. Pregnancy test is negative. She is otherwise well and can take oral medicine. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Intramuscular ceftriaxone then oral doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days
questions.e: Pelvic inflammatory disease is treated empirically to cover gonorrhoea, chlamydia and anaerobes, for example ceftriaxone followed by doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days. Delay or inadequate cover increases the risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

questions.s: A 24-year-old woman being treated for pelvic inflammatory disease develops right upper quadrant pain that is worse on deep breathing. Liver function tests and gallbladder ultrasound are normal. What is the most likely cause?
questions.e: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is inflammation of the liver capsule with adhesions, complicating chlamydial or gonococcal PID and causing pleuritic right upper quadrant pain with normal liver tests. Normal ultrasound argues against cholecystitis.

questions.s: A 27-year-old woman has a single painless, clean-based, indurated ulcer on the labium minus for 10 days, with bilateral non-tender rubbery inguinal lymph nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A painless, indurated ulcer with non-tender lymphadenopathy is the chancre of primary syphilis, confirmed by dark-ground microscopy or serology. Herpes and chancroid both cause painful ulcers, chancroid with tender suppurating nodes.

questions.s: Sobia, 15, has not started her periods. She is 138 cm tall with a webbed neck, widely spaced nipples and absent breast development. FSH is markedly raised. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Short stature, webbed neck, absent puberty and high FSH from streak ovaries suggest Turner syndrome (45,X), confirmed by karyotype. Constitutional delay and Kallmann syndrome give low gonadotropins.

questions.s: A 34-year-old woman has had no periods for 7 months, with hot flushes and night sweats. Pregnancy test is negative and FSH is raised on two occasions 6 weeks apart. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Reassurance, as no treatment is needed before 45 years
Hormone replacement until the average age of menopause
questions.e: Premature ovarian insufficiency before 40 years is diagnosed by amenorrhoea with raised FSH on two occasions, and hormone replacement (HRT or combined pill) is advised until about 51 years to protect bones and the heart. Clomifene cannot stimulate failed ovaries.

questions.s: A 20-year-old university athlete has had no periods for 8 months. Her BMI is 17 and she trains intensively. Pregnancy test is negative. Which hormone pattern is most likely?
o: High FSH, high LH, low oestradiol
Normal FSH, high LH, high testosterone
Low FSH, low LH, low oestradiol
questions.e: Low body weight and excessive exercise suppress GnRH pulsatility, causing functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea with low gonadotropins and low oestrogen, which risks bone loss. High FSH would indicate ovarian failure, and a high LH with androgen excess suggests PCOS.

questions.s: Fiza, 14, has monthly lower abdominal pain for 6 months but has never menstruated. Secondary sexual characteristics are normal. Examination shows a tense, bluish bulging membrane at the introitus. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Cyclical pain without menstruation and a bulging bluish membrane at the introitus is typical of an imperforate hymen with menstrual blood collected in the vagina; a cruciate incision is curative. A transverse septum lies higher and does not bulge at the introitus.

questions.s: A 48-year-old obese woman has had irregular heavy bleeding with intermenstrual bleeding for 6 months. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an endometrial thickness of 16 mm. What is the most appropriate next step?
o: Start the combined oral contraceptive pill
Tranexamic acid and review in 6 months
questions.e: Persistent intermenstrual bleeding in a woman over 45 with obesity and a thickened endometrium requires endometrial sampling, by pipelle or hysteroscopy, to exclude hyperplasia or cancer. Treating symptoms without histology may delay a cancer diagnosis.

questions.s: A couple has been trying to conceive for 18 months. The wife has regular cycles. Which is the first investigation for the husband?
questions.e: Semen analysis is the first and most important test of male fertility and should be done early because male factors contribute to many infertile couples. Hormone tests and imaging are guided by an abnormal result.

questions.s: Sidra, 18, has primary amenorrhoea and poor breast development. She cannot smell perfume or food. FSH, LH and oestradiol are all low. MRI of the pituitary is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia is Kallmann syndrome, due to failed migration of GnRH neurones with olfactory neurones. Turner syndrome causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, and a normal MRI excludes a prolactinoma.

questions.s: A 37-year-old woman considering IVF asks how her remaining egg supply can be assessed. Which test best estimates ovarian reserve?
questions.e: Anti-Müllerian hormone, produced by small ovarian follicles, correlates with the remaining follicle pool and predicts response to stimulation; antral follicle count is an alternative. Mid-luteal progesterone confirms ovulation, not reserve.

questions.s: The husband of an infertile couple has a soft swelling above the left testis that feels like a bag of worms on standing and disappears on lying down. Semen analysis shows reduced motility. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A varicocele is dilatation of the pampiniform plexus, usually on the left because the left testicular vein drains at a right angle into the renal vein; it may impair semen quality. A hydrocele transilluminates and surrounds the testis.

questions.s: A 26-year-old woman attends for copper IUD insertion. Speculum examination shows a purulent discharge from the cervical os and the cervix bleeds on contact. What is the most appropriate action?
o: Postpone insertion, test for STIs and treat
Insert the IUD with antibiotic cover
Insert the IUD and review in 6 weeks
Offer the device only after a hysteroscopy
questions.e: Current purulent cervicitis or PID is a contraindication to IUD insertion because of the risk of ascending infection; she should be tested and treated first, using another method meanwhile. Inserting the device in the presence of infection risks PID.

questions.s: A 22-year-old woman has a subdermal etonogestrel implant fitted. For how long is it licensed to provide contraception?
questions.e: The etonogestrel implant is licensed for 3 years and is one of the most effective reversible methods. Ten years applies to some copper IUDs.

questions.s: A woman who had a contraceptive implant fitted 4 months ago asks about its most common side effect. What is it?
questions.e: Unpredictable bleeding is the commonest reason for implant removal; some women have amenorrhoea and others frequent or prolonged bleeding. Fertility returns promptly after removal, unlike after the depot injection.

questions.s: A 30-year-old woman asks about non-contraceptive benefits of the combined oral contraceptive pill. Which benefit is well established?
o: Reduced risk of ovarian and endometrial cancer
Reduced risk of venous thromboembolism and stroke
questions.e: The combined pill reduces the risk of ovarian and endometrial cancer, an effect that persists for years after stopping. It slightly increases the risks of venous thromboembolism, and of breast and cervical cancer with long use.

questions.s: How is the Pearl index, used to compare the effectiveness of contraceptive methods, defined?
o: Number of women who stop a method within one year
Percentage of women satisfied with the method
questions.e: The Pearl index is the number of unintended pregnancies per 100 woman-years of exposure; a lower value means a more effective method. Discontinuation rates measure acceptability, not effectiveness.

questions.s: A 24-year-old woman with PCOS has dark, velvety thickened skin in her axillae and on the back of her neck. What does this finding reflect?
questions.e: Acanthosis nigricans is a skin marker of insulin resistance and hyperinsulinaemia, common in PCOS and obesity, and should prompt glucose screening. Adrenal insufficiency causes generalised pigmentation, not velvety thickening.

questions.s: Which scoring system is commonly used to grade hirsutism in women with PCOS?
questions.e: The modified Ferriman-Gallwey score rates terminal hair growth at nine body sites. Tanner staging describes pubertal development and the Bishop score assesses the cervix before induction.

questions.s: Using the Rotterdam criteria, and once other causes are excluded, which set of findings is sufficient for a diagnosis of PCOS?
o: Oligo-ovulation and polycystic ovarian morphology without hyperandrogenism
Hirsutism alone with regular ovulatory cycles
questions.e: Rotterdam criteria need two of three: oligo- or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology, after excluding other causes. Obesity and LH:FSH ratio are not part of the criteria.

questions.s: Kiran, 29, with PCOS is starting clomifene to induce ovulation. Which risk should she be counselled about?
questions.e: Ovulation induction with clomifene can cause multiple follicle development and twin pregnancy, so ultrasound monitoring is advised, at least in the first cycle. It is not associated with fetal malformation or premature menopause.

questions.s: From which tissue do uterine fibroids arise?
questions.e: Leiomyomas are benign monoclonal tumours of myometrial smooth muscle cells with a fibrous component. Endometrial glands and stroma growing within the myometrium constitute adenomyosis.

questions.s: A 54-year-old woman with known fibroids asks what will happen to them now that her periods have stopped. Why do fibroids usually shrink after menopause?
o: Loss of ovarian oestrogen and progesterone
questions.e: Fibroid growth depends on oestrogen and progesterone, so they shrink after menopause as ovarian hormone production falls, and grow during pregnancy. Calcification may follow regression but does not cause it.

questions.s: A 45-year-old woman with symptomatic multiple fibroids has completed her family. She wishes to keep her uterus and avoid major surgery. What is the most appropriate option?
questions.e: Uterine artery embolisation is a minimally invasive, uterus-sparing option for women with fibroids who have completed their family. Long-term GnRH agonists cause bone loss and are used only for a short time.

questions.s: Tranexamic acid is prescribed for a woman with heavy menstrual bleeding due to small fibroids. How does it reduce menstrual blood loss?
questions.e: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic that blocks plasminogen activation, reducing endometrial clot breakdown and blood loss by about half. NSAIDs act by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis.

questions.s: A 58-year-old woman notices a bulge in the vagina and feels she does not empty her bladder fully. Examination shows descent of the anterior vaginal wall on straining. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Anterior vaginal wall prolapse containing the bladder is a cystocele, causing urinary symptoms such as incomplete emptying. A rectocele involves the posterior wall and causes difficulty in defecation.

questions.s: A 70-year-old woman uses a ring pessary for uterine prolapse. At her review the vaginal walls are thin and pale with a small erosion. What should be added to reduce this problem?
questions.e: Vaginal atrophy after menopause predisposes to pessary-related erosion, and topical vaginal oestrogen improves tissue quality. Systemic HRT is not needed for this purpose, and douching may cause irritation.

questions.s: A 76-year-old woman has had complete procidentia for many years. She now has reduced urine output and a raised serum creatinine. Ultrasound shows bilateral hydronephrosis. What is the most likely mechanism?
o: Kinking and obstruction of the ureters
questions.e: With complete uterine procidentia the bladder base and ureters are drawn down outside the pelvis, kinking and obstructing the ureters and causing hydronephrosis. Reducing the prolapse, with a pessary or surgery, relieves the obstruction.

questions.s: A 52-year-old woman has a sudden strong urge to pass urine, often leaking before reaching the toilet, with frequency and nocturia. Urine dipstick is normal. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
o: Bladder training for at least 6 weeks
questions.e: Overactive bladder with urge incontinence is treated first with bladder training and lifestyle measures, then antimuscarinic or beta-3 agonist drugs. Sling surgery and colposuspension are for stress incontinence.

questions.s: A mother asks about HPV vaccination for her daughter. At what time is the vaccine most effective?
o: After the first abnormal cervical screen
At the age of 50, before menopause
Before the onset of sexual activity, ideally age 9 to 14
questions.e: HPV vaccines prevent infection rather than treat it, so they are most effective before any exposure; WHO prioritises girls aged 9 to 14. The vaccine does not treat existing infection or CIN.

questions.s: A 34-year-old woman with high-risk HPV on screening has colposcopy, and biopsy confirms CIN 3. What is the most appropriate management?
o: Large loop excision of the transformation zone
questions.e: CIN 3 is a high-grade pre-invasive lesion treated by excision of the transformation zone, usually LLETZ, followed by test-of-cure HPV testing. Radical hysterectomy and chemoradiotherapy are treatments for invasive cancer.

questions.s: A 63-year-old woman is diagnosed with endometrial carcinoma after postmenopausal bleeding. What is the most common histological type?
questions.e: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the commonest type and is linked to unopposed oestrogen, obesity and hyperplasia, usually with a good prognosis when found early. Serous and clear cell types are more aggressive and less common.

questions.s: A 45-year-old woman with weight loss and epigastric discomfort has bilateral solid ovarian masses. Histology shows mucin-filled signet ring cells. Where is the most likely primary tumour?
questions.e: Krukenberg tumours are bilateral ovarian metastases with signet ring cells, most commonly from gastric carcinoma, followed by colorectal and breast. Endometrial cancer spreads to the ovary but does not produce signet ring cells.

questions.s: A 60-year-old woman has a solid right ovarian mass, ascites and a right pleural effusion. CA-125 is mildly raised. After removal of the ovarian tumour, the ascites and effusion resolve. Histology shows a benign tumour. What is the most likely diagnosis?
o: Meigs syndrome due to ovarian fibroma
questions.e: Meigs syndrome is the triad of a benign ovarian fibroma, ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after removal of the tumour. Stage IV ovarian carcinoma would show malignant cells and would not resolve with simple removal.

questions.s: A 22-year-old woman has a positive NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis on a swab taken for post-coital bleeding. She is not pregnant and has no allergies. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: Doxycycline for 7 days is first-line for uncomplicated chlamydia, with partner notification and treatment; azithromycin is an alternative, especially in pregnancy. Metronidazole has no activity against chlamydia.

questions.s: A 25-year-old woman has a purulent cervical discharge. Gram stain shows intracellular Gram-negative diplococci. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Oral ciprofloxacin as a single dose
questions.e: Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci indicate gonorrhoea, treated with intramuscular ceftriaxone, with testing for chlamydia and other infections. Resistance to ciprofloxacin and penicillins is widespread, so they are not used empirically.

questions.s: A 28-year-old woman has a painful, tender, fluctuant swelling in the posterior part of the right labium majus, making walking and sitting difficult. What is the most appropriate treatment?
o: Total excision of the gland as the first step
Incision with marsupialisation or a Word catheter
questions.e: A Bartholin abscess needs drainage, by marsupialisation or a Word catheter to reduce recurrence; antibiotics alone rarely resolve a fluctuant abscess. Excision of the gland is reserved for recurrent cases.

questions.s: Two days after vaginal surgery with a vaginal pack left in place, a 35-year-old woman has fever of 39.5 °C, a diffuse red macular rash, vomiting, diarrhoea and BP 80/45 mmHg. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Toxic shock syndrome follows toxin-producing Staphylococcus aureus colonising a retained foreign body such as a pack or tampon, causing fever, diffuse erythroderma, shock and multi-organ involvement. The pack must be removed and antibiotics and resuscitation started.
